> I couldn't reproduce on my xfce, what desktop manager is your ubuntu using, gnome?

@amrbashir Yes.

Hello, I had the same issue with **Tauri v2.0.6** on **Ubuntu 22.04**. I tried everything, like adding `StartupWMClass` to the `.desktop` file and clearing icon caches, but nothing worked.

What finally fixed it was **disabling Wayland** by uncommenting `WaylandEnable=false` in `/etc/gdm3/custom.conf`. After switching to **Xorg**, the icon showed up correctly in the dock.

Not sure why Wayland with Tauri causes this issue, but if anyone has insights or a workaround for Wayland, I’d love to know.

The dev version will create it in `~/.local/share/applications`

In my experience, the dev version file has `Exec, Name` as entries but does not have Icon, while the installed version does.

Apologies for the delayed response, everyone.

From my experience even after installing the application the icon was missing on both Ubuntu 22 and 24. I haven’t tested this recently as I haven’t worked with Tauri in a while

This is the exact solution I was referring to earlier what @yunger7 suggested is in my opinion the best implementation for this scenario. It’s important to note that the startupWMClass value should match the Tauri app name as defined in your .toml file. That said this should ideally be handled by Tauri itself rather than requiring developers to implement such workarounds manually.

issue.body:
closes #5258

Spinned off a Fedora VM to test Museeks, and realized the icon would never show in dock, nor the installer. Modern Fedora uses Wayland. This also applied to Ubuntu. Forcing x11 shown the correct icon.

For whatever reasons, setting `StartupWMClass` to the name of the app fixes it. See the discussion linked above. I don't know if this is just Gnome, or Freedesktop or whatever, but this fixes it.

but is showing correctly in dock + grid view:

![Screenshot 2025-06-06 at 15 00 22](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6790b45-9966-4f9e-bbb4-f498f76b9c83)
